## Requirement conflict, not a guessed replacement

No host loops is mandatory, including the recorded pool `/dev/loop0`; no detach or migration is authorized. Subvolume-only is conditional. Native Incus Btrfs filesystem volumes are subvolumes, but a subvolume is not the writable block member of true Btrfs seeding/sprouting. A real non-loop block device can satisfy device-add; supplied evidence does not identify an authorized allocation.

Upstream Btrfs documentation says that since kernel 6.17 the same seed device cannot be mounted standalone and through a sprout simultaneously. Recorded kernel is 6.18. The permanently mounted seed requirement therefore requires explicit topology resolution. Distinct non-loop views such as device-mapper linear are research candidates only, not proven workarounds. Do not infer that native Incus cannot run sprouts: historical external root binding did so, using loops. [recovery/NativeFeasibility.md, https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html]
